title: Gacha Simulation: Pity Mechanics and Probability Psychology
subtitle: This guide dissects the structural differences between hard and soft pity systems, analyzing how probability psychology creates perceived bias. Through simulation verification of gacha data, we reveal how emotional thresholds impact decision-making, helping developers quantify pity strategy risks and optimize numerical design to boost user retention and willingness to pay.

breakdown.title: Pity Structure (Most Common)
bullets: Hard Pity: Guaranteed target rarity after N pulls
Soft Pity: Probability increases as you approach N (better perceived experience)
Targeted Mechanism: Hard pity reset or guaranteed next pull if missed, reducing the feeling of being 'backstabbed'

breakdown.title: Probability Psychology
bullets: Players remember 'streaks of failure', not the mean
Soft pity significantly reduces the tail probability of long failure streaks
Clearing the rules actually reduces controversy (players fear the black box)

breakdown.title: Simulation and Verification
bullets: Analyze distribution rather than just expectation: Pulls needed for P50/P90/P99
Compare 'Pure Random vs Soft Pity' to observe the ratio of extreme non-guaranteed users
Monitor churn points: Retention drops when consecutive failures exceed a threshold
